p.src: When Xifeng heard what the little maid had said, anger, anxiety, and grief overwhelmed her. She suddenly coughed up a mouthful of blood, fainted, and collapsed to the floor. Pinger hurried over to support her and called for help. They slowly carried Xifeng to her own room, laid her gently on the kang, and Pinger at once told Xiaohong to pour a cup of hot water and hold it to her lips. Xifeng took a sip but remained unconscious and lay sleeping. Qiutong came over, took a cursory look, and walked away; Pinger did not call her back. Seeing Fenger standing nearby, Pinger told her to go at once and clearly report to Ladies Xing and Wang that Second Mistress Lian had vomited blood and fainted and could attend to nothing. Lady Xing supposed that Xifeng was feigning illness to shirk her duties. Since many female relatives were present, she could say nothing more, but she did not entirely believe the report and merely said, “Tell her to go and rest.” No one else said anything. Visitors came and went without cease that evening, but fortunately several close female relatives were there to receive them. When the household servants saw that Xifeng was absent, some stole a little leisure and rested from their work. Amid the noise and confusion, everything was soon in utter disorder and nothing was being properly done. After the guests from afar departed sometime after the second watch, preparations began for the final farewell before the coffin. The women within the mourning enclosure all wept for a time. Yuanyang had wept herself unconscious. The others supported her and thumped and fussed over her until she revived, whereupon she said, “The Old Lady cherished me all these years; I shall follow her.” They all assumed that grief commonly made people say such things and paid no heed. When the time came to take leave of the departed, there were well over a hundred people from every rank of the household, but Yuanyang was nowhere to be seen. In all the bustle, however, who had time to check the attendance? When it was time for Amber and the other maids to weep and make their offerings, Yuanyang was still absent. They supposed that she had exhausted herself with crying and was resting somewhere else for a while, so they said nothing. After the farewell ceremony, Jia Zheng summoned Jia Lian outside and questioned him about the funeral procession, then began discussing whom they should leave to guard the house. Jia Lian replied, “Among the masters, Yun is to remain at home and see to things instead of joining the funeral procession; among the servants, Lin Zhixiao’s whole family is to oversee the dismantling of the awnings and such work. But I do not know which woman is to be left in charge inside.” Jia Zheng said, “I heard your mother say that your wife is ill and cannot go, so she is to remain at home. Your elder sister-in-law Zhen also said that your wife was seriously ill, and that Fourth Girl should stay with her and lead a few maids and matrons in looking after the principal apartments.” Hearing this, Jia Lian thought, “Elder Sister-in-law Zhen and Fourth Girl do not get along, so she has urged them not to let the girl go. But even if she is left to manage the principal apartments, she will be of little use. And my own wife is ill, so she can hardly take charge either.”

p.src: Meanwhile, after weeping for a time, Yuanyang thought, “I served the Old Lady all my life, yet now I have nowhere to turn. Though the Elder Master is away from home, I cannot abide the way the Elder Mistress behaves. Master Zheng never concerns himself with household affairs. Once everyone begins ruling amid the chaos, will not people like us be left for them to manipulate as they please? One may take me as a concubine, another may marry me to some servant boy. I cannot bear such torment; I would be better off cleanly dead. But how am I to die at such short notice?” Thinking as she went, she returned to the inner room adjoining the Old Lady’s chamber. She had just crossed the threshold when, in the dismal lamplight, she dimly saw a woman holding a handkerchief as though she meant to hang herself. Yuanyang felt no fear or surprise, but thought, “Who can she be? She has the same intention as I do, but has gone ahead of me.” She asked, “Who are you? We are of one mind; if we are to die, let us die together.” The woman made no reply. Yuanyang went closer and saw that she was not one of the maids from that apartment. As she looked more carefully, a penetrating chill swept over her, and the figure vanished. Yuanyang stood dazed for a moment, then withdrew and sat on the edge of the kang. After thinking carefully, she said to herself, “Oh, I see! That was Young Mistress Rong from the Eastern Mansion! She died long ago, so why has she come here? She must have come to summon me. But why was she hanging herself?” After another moment’s thought, she said, “Of course—she must have come to show me how to die.” Once this thought took hold of Yuanyang, the evil influence sank into her bones. She rose, and as she wept, opened her dressing case, took out the lock of hair she had cut off that year, and tucked it into her bosom. Then she untied a handkerchief from her person and fastened it at the spot Qin-shi had just indicated. After weeping once more, she heard the guests outside dispersing. Fearing that someone might enter, she hurriedly barred the door, brought over a footstool, and stood upon it. She tied a noose in the handkerchief, slipped it around her throat, and kicked the stool away. Alas, her breath ceased in her throat and her fragrant soul left its mortal shell. With nowhere to go, it saw Qin-shi dimly ahead. Yuanyang’s spirit hastened after her, calling, “Young Mistress Rong, wait for me!” The figure replied, “I am no Young Mistress Rong. I am Keqing, younger sister of the Disenchantment Fairy.” Yuanyang said, “But you are plainly Young Mistress Rong. Why do you say you are not?” The figure said, “There is a reason for that. Once I tell you, you will understand.”

p.src: In the Palace of Disenchantment, I was once the chief votary of devotion, charged with all debts of love and passion. When I descended into the mortal world, I was naturally to be the foremost of faithful lovers and guide these infatuated, aggrieved women early into the Department of Love; thus it was ordained that I should hang myself. But because I saw through mortal passions, crossed beyond the sea of emotion, and returned to the heaven of love, the Department of Infatuation in the Land of Illusion of the Great Void was left entirely without a keeper. Now the Fairy Disenchantment has appointed you to fill the vacancy and take charge of that department in my stead, so she ordered me to come and lead you there.” Yuanyang’s spirit said, “I am the most unfeeling of women. How can I be counted among those who possess true feeling?” The other replied, “There is much you still do not understand. People in the world all mistake carnal desire for ‘love’; they commit acts that corrupt morals and debase custom, yet call themselves passionate devotees of romance and dismiss it as a matter of no consequence. They do not know that what is called ‘feeling,’ before joy, anger, sorrow, or pleasure has arisen, is our nature; once joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure have arisen, it becomes emotion. As for the feeling you and I possess, it is precisely feeling before it has stirred, like a flower still in bud. If it seeks release and expression, it ceases to be true feeling.” Yuanyang’s spirit heard this, nodded in understanding, and followed Qin Keqing away.

p.src: Meanwhile, after Hupo had taken leave of the mourning hall and heard Madams Xing and Wang assigning people to guard the house, she thought she should ask Yuanyang which carriage she was to ride in the next day. Unable to find her after searching Grandmother Jia’s outer room, she went into the inner chamber. Just as she reached the doorway, she saw that the door was ajar. Peering through the crack, she could make out only the dim, flickering lamplight and vague shadows. Frightened at heart and hearing no sound from within, she turned back, saying, “Where has that wretch run off to?” She immediately ran into Zhenzhu and asked, “Have you seen Sister Yuanyang?” Zhenzhu replied, “I’m looking for her too. The mistresses are waiting to speak with her. She must have fallen asleep in the inner chamber.” Hupo said, “I looked, but there was no one in the room. No one had even trimmed the lampwick, and it was so dark and frightening that I did not go in. Let us go in together now and see whether she is there.” Hupo and the others went in and were trimming the lampwick when Zhenzhu said, “Who left this footstool here? I nearly tripped over it.” As she spoke, she looked up. With a terrified cry of “Ai-yo!” she reeled backward and fell heavily against Hupo. Hupo saw it too and began shrieking, but her feet were rooted to the spot.

p.src: The people outside heard them and rushed in to look. Everyone cried out that Madams Xing and Wang must be informed. When Lady Wang, Baochai, and the others heard, they went weeping to see for themselves. Lady Xing said, “I never expected Yuanyang to have such resolution. Quickly, send someone to tell the master.” Baoyu alone, on hearing the news, was so horrified that his eyes stared rigidly before him. Xiren and the others hurriedly supported him, saying, “If you need to cry, then cry. Do not hold your breath in.” Only with a desperate effort did Baoyu finally manage to weep. He thought, “That a person like Yuanyang should meet such a death!” Then he thought, “Truly, all the spiritual essence between heaven and earth is concentrated in women such as these. She has found a worthy place in death, while we are, after all, no more than foul things. Though we are the Old Lady’s own sons and grandsons, which of us can compare with her?” At this, he became happy again. By then Baochai had heard Baoyu wailing and had come out too; but when she reached him, she found him laughing again. Xiren and the others hastily said, “This is bad—he is going mad again.” Baochai said, “It is nothing. He has his own reasons.” Hearing this, Baoyu was even more delighted by Baochai’s words. “She, at least, still understands my heart. How could anyone else know?” While he was lost in these wild thoughts, Jia Zheng and the others came in. They sighed deeply and said, “What a good girl! The Old Lady’s affection for her was not bestowed in vain!” He immediately ordered Jia Lian to go out and have someone buy a coffin that very night and lay her in it. “Tomorrow she shall be borne out with the Old Lady’s funeral procession, and her coffin shall be placed behind the Old Lady’s, so that her devotion may be fulfilled.” Jia Lian assented and went out. Meanwhile, they had Yuanyang taken down and laid in the inner room. When Ping’er learned of it, she came over, and together with Xiren, Ying’er, and all the others, wept until they were nearly overcome with grief. Among them, Zijuan reflected that she herself had no secure place in life. “If only I had followed Miss Lin in death! I would have fulfilled the bond of devotion between mistress and maid and also found a worthy end. Now I merely hang in uncertainty in Baoyu’s rooms. Though Baoyu still treats me with tender affection, what does it ultimately amount to?” At this, she wept with still greater anguish.

p.src: Lady Wang promptly summoned Yuanyang's sister-in-law and told her to attend the encoffining. After consulting Lady Xing, she granted the sister-in-law a hundred taels of silver from the old lady's estate and said that, when things quieted down, all Yuanyang's belongings would also be given to her family. Her sister-in-law kowtowed and went out, saying delightedly, “Our girl truly had spirit and good fortune! She has won a fine name and been given a splendid funeral besides.” An old serving woman nearby said, “Enough, sister! You are this pleased to have sold a living girl for a hundred taels. If she had been given to the eldest master back then, who knows how much silver you might have received? You would have been prouder still!” The remark struck the sister-in-law to the heart; she flushed and walked away. Just as she reached the inner gate, she saw Lin Zhixiao leading men in with the coffin. She had no choice but to follow them back and help with the laying out, making a show of wailing a few times. Because Yuanyang had died for Grandmother Jia, Jia Zheng asked for incense, offered three sticks, bowed, and said, “She died in devotion to her mistress and must not be treated as a mere maid. All of you younger people should pay your respects.” Baoyu was overjoyed to hear this. He stepped forward and reverently kowtowed several times. Remembering all her kindness in former days, Jia Lian also meant to come forward and bow, but Lady Xing said, “One gentleman is enough. Do not burden her with more honors than she can bear and keep her from attaining rebirth.” Jia Lian therefore could not very well approach. Baochai felt deeply uncomfortable on hearing this and said, “It is true that I ought not to bow to her. But when the old lady died, all of us still had duties left undone and dared not act rashly. Since Yuanyang was willing to fulfill our filial duty for us, we should at least commend the old lady to her care and ask her to serve her well on the journey west. That would let us show a little of what is in our hearts.” With that, she took Yinger's arm and went before the bier. As she poured the libation, tears were already streaming down her face. When the offering was finished, she bowed several times and wept bitterly for Yuanyang. Some said that Baoyu and his wife were both fools; some said that the two of them were kindhearted; still others said that they understood propriety. Jia Zheng, for his part, was pleased. It was settled that Xifeng and Xichun would again remain to watch the house, while everyone else would be sent to accompany the coffin. No one dared sleep that night. At the fifth watch, they heard the people assembling outside. At the beginning of the hour of the dragon, the funeral procession set out. As the senior mourner, Jia Zheng wore hempen mourning clothes and wept, observing to the utmost every rite required of a filial son. Once the coffin had passed through the gate, various families made roadside offerings. There is no need to describe in detail the splendor along the way. After traveling for half a day, they reached Iron Threshold Temple and installed the coffin there. All the mourning sons and the others were to spend the night accompanying it in the temple. No more need be said of them.

p.src: Back at the house, Lin Zhixiao supervised the dismantling of the awnings, secured the doors and windows, had the courtyards swept clean, and assigned watchmen to sound the watches and keep guard that night. The Rong mansion's rule, however, was that after the first and second watches the three inner gates were shut, so that no men could enter; within, only the women made the night rounds. Although Xifeng had recovered some of her spirits after a night's rest, she was still in no condition to move about. Only Pinger and Xichun went around the various quarters, gave instructions to those on night duty, and then each returned to her room. Now Zhou Rui's godson, He San, had fought with Bao Er the previous year while Jia Zhen was managing affairs. Jia Zhen had beaten him and driven him out, and ever since he had spent his days in gambling dens. Recently, hearing that Grandmother Jia had died, he assumed there would be errands from which he could profit. But after sounding things out for several days and finding no opportunity at all, he returned to the gambling den sighing and sat down dejectedly. The others asked him, “Well, Third Brother, how did it go? Aren't you joining us to win back your losses?” He San said, “I would like to win some back, but I haven't any money.” They said, “You spent several days with that great patron of yours, Master Zhou. Who knows how much money you got out of the mansion? And now you are pretending to be poor with us again.” He San said, “Don't remind me! They have millions in gold and silver, heaven knows how much, yet they only hoard it and never spend it. One day it will either burn in a fire or be stolen by thieves; only then will they be satisfied.” The others said, “You are lying again. Their property was confiscated—how much gold and silver could they still have?” He San said, “You do not understand. What was confiscated was only what they could not hide away. Now that the old lady is dead, she has left a great deal of gold and silver. None of them will touch it; it is all stored in her rooms, to be divided when they return from the funeral.” One of the men took this to heart. After throwing the dice a few more times, he said, “I have lost a little money, but I will not try to win it back. I am going to bed.” With that he went outside, pulled He San aside, and said, “Third Brother, I want a word with you.” He San followed him out. u.src: Back at the house, Lin Zhixiao supervised the dismantling of the awnings, secured the doors and windows, had the courtyards swept clean, and assigned watchmen to sound the watches and keep guard that night.
The Rong mansion's rule, however, was that after the first and second watches the three inner gates were shut, so that no men could enter; within, only the women made the night rounds.
Although Xifeng had recovered some of her spirits after a night's rest, she was still in no condition to move about.
Only Pinger and Xichun went around the various quarters, gave instructions to those on night duty, and then each returned to her room.

Now Zhou Rui's godson, He San, had fought with Bao Er the previous year while Jia Zhen was managing affairs. Jia Zhen had beaten him and driven him out, and ever since he had spent his days in gambling dens.

Recently, hearing that Grandmother Jia had died, he assumed there would be errands from which he could profit. But after sounding things out for several days and finding no opportunity at all, he returned to the gambling den sighing and sat down dejectedly.
The others asked him, “Well, Third Brother, how did it go?
Aren't you joining us to win back your losses?”
He San said, “I would like to win some back, but I haven't any money.”
They said, “You spent several days with that great patron of yours, Master Zhou. Who knows how much money you got out of the mansion? And now you are pretending to be poor with us again.”
He San said, “Don't remind me! They have millions in gold and silver, heaven knows how much, yet they only hoard it and never spend it.
One day it will either burn in a fire or be stolen by thieves; only then will they be satisfied.”
The others said, “You are lying again. Their property was confiscated—how much gold and silver could they still have?”
He San said, “You do not understand. What was confiscated was only what they could not hide away.
Now that the old lady is dead, she has left a great deal of gold and silver. None of them will touch it; it is all stored in her rooms, to be divided when they return from the funeral.”

p.src: The man said, “I told you that you were no good at this. I have a good many friends with extraordinary skills. Never mind that they have all gone with the funeral procession and only a few women remain at home—we would not be afraid even if any number of men were there. I only doubt that you have the nerve for it.” He San said, “What do you mean, whether I dare or not? Do you imagine I am afraid of that godfather of mine? I acknowledged him as my godfather only out of regard for my godmother. He is hardly worth calling a man! The only trouble with what you just proposed is that if we fail to get the goods, we shall land ourselves in a terrible mess. Is there any government office they are not well connected with? Even if we did manage to take it, to say nothing of failing, they would be sure to raise an uproar over it.” The man said, “If that is all, then your good fortune has arrived. Some of my friends are from the coast. They are all here now, watching for an opportunity and waiting for a way in. Once the goods are in our hands, there will be no profit in our staying here. How does that sound?” He San said, “Brother, you must be drunk. What nonsense are you talking?” As he spoke, he pulled the man aside to a secluded place. The two conferred for a while and then went their separate ways. We shall leave them for the present.

p.src: Now, ever since Jia Zheng had angrily sent Bao Yong to guard the garden, the household had grown busy with Grandmother Jia’s death, and no duty had been assigned to him. He paid no heed to this, but cooked and ate for himself, slept whenever he felt bored, and upon waking amused himself in the garden with swords and staffs, living quite free of restraint. Early on the day of Grandmother Jia’s funeral, although he knew what was happening, no duty had been assigned to him, so he wandered about at his leisure. He saw a Buddhist nun accompanied by a Taoist woman come to the side gate inside the garden and knock. Bao Yong went over and asked, “Where are you going, Reverend Mother?” The Taoist woman replied, “We heard that the old lady’s funeral was held today, yet we did not see the Fourth Young Lady join the procession. She must have remained at home to watch the house. Thinking she might be lonely, our mistress has come to pay her a visit.” Bao Yong said, “None of the masters is at home, and I am guarding the garden gate. Please go back. If you wish to come, return after the masters have come home.” The old woman said, “Where did a black lump of coal like you come from, that you should presume to control our comings and goings?” Bao Yong said, “I cannot abide people like you. If I refuse to let you in, what can you do about it?” The woman flew into a rage and shouted, “The whole world has been turned upside down! Even while the old lady was alive, she never barred us from coming and going. What overbearing bandit are you, to behave with such utter disregard for law and heaven? I am determined to go in through this gate!” With that, she struck the door ring hard several times with her hand. Miaoyu was too angry to speak and was just turning to leave when the old woman guarding the inner gate, hearing what sounded like a quarrel, opened it to look. She saw Miaoyu already walking away and knew at once that Bao Yong must have offended her and driven her off. The old women had lately all learned that the ladies of the house and the Fourth Young Lady were very close to her. Fearing that if Miaoyu later reported that she had been denied entry at the gate, they would be unable to bear the blame, the gatekeeper hurried after her and said, “We did not know you had come, Reverend Mother, and were slow to open the gate. Our Fourth Young Lady is at home and has been thinking of you. Please come back at once. The fellow guarding the garden is newly arrived and knows nothing of our arrangements. When the ladies return, we shall report him, have him beaten, and drive him out, and that will be the end of it.” Although Miaoyu heard her, she paid no attention. But the woman guarding the side gate caught up with her and pleaded again and again. At last she confessed that she feared being held to blame herself and, in her distress, almost went down on her knees. Miaoyu, having no other choice, finally followed her back. Seeing how matters stood, Bao Yong naturally could not bar her way. He went back glaring and sighing with rage.

p.src: Miaoyu and the Taoist nun went to Xichun’s quarters, apologized for disturbing her, and chatted for a while. Xichun said, “Staying home to watch the house means little more than enduring a few sleepless nights. But Second Mistress is ill, and being alone leaves me both lonely and frightened; I would feel at ease if someone could stay here with me. There is not a single man in the inner quarters now. Since you have honored me with a visit today, would you stay the night, play chess, and talk with me?” Miaoyu was reluctant at first, but she pitied Xichun, and the mention of chess put her in such good spirits that she agreed. She sent the Taoist nun back for her tea utensils, clothes, and bedding, had an attendant bring them over, and they sat talking through the night. Xichun was delighted beyond measure and ordered Caiping to open the jar of rainwater collected the previous year and prepare fine tea. Miaoyu had brought her own tea service. Not long after the Taoist nun left, another attendant arrived carrying Miaoyu’s daily necessities. Xichun brewed the tea herself. The two found each other congenial and talked for a long while. By the first watch, Caiping had set out the board, and they began a game of go. Xichun lost two games in succession. Only after Miaoyu gave her a four-stone handicap did Xichun win by half a point. By then it was the fourth watch; beneath the boundless sky, not a sound could be heard. Miaoyu said, “At the fifth watch I must meditate for a while. I have someone to attend me, so you should go and rest.” Xichun was still reluctant to leave, but seeing that Miaoyu wished to compose her spirit, she could not press her. Just as she was about to retire, a chorus of shouts suddenly rose from the night watch in the main rooms to the east. The old women in Xichun’s quarters took up the cry: “This is terrible! Someone has broken in!” Xichun, Caiping, and the others were frightened out of their wits, while the men keeping watch outside also began shouting at the tops of their voices. Miaoyu said, “This is bad. There must be thieves here.” As she spoke, no one dared open the door, and they screened the lamplight. Someone peered through a crack in the window and saw several men standing in the courtyard. Too frightened to utter a sound, she turned, waved her hands, climbed softly down, and whispered, “This is dreadful—there are several burly men outside.” Before she had finished speaking, a continual clatter sounded from the roof, and the men keeping watch outside came in, shouting for everyone to catch the thieves. One man said, “Everything in the main rooms is gone, but there is no one in sight. Someone went off toward the east; let us go west.” Hearing that their own people had arrived, Xichun’s old women called from the outer room, “Several men have climbed onto the roof here.” The night watchmen cried, “Look—there they are!” Everyone began shouting at once. A shower of roof tiles came flying down, and no one dared advance.

p.src: While they stood helpless, there came a tremendous crash from the side gate of the garden. The gate was forced open, and in strode a tall, lanky fellow wielding a wooden staff. Everyone was so frightened that they had no time to hide. They heard the man shout, “Do not let a single one of them escape! All of you, follow me!” Hearing this, the servants were more terrified than ever; their limbs went limp, and they could not even run. The man stood there shouting incessantly until one sharp-eyed servant recognized him. And who should it be but Baoyong, the man recommended by the Zhen family? The servants immediately recovered some courage and said in trembling voices, “One of them has gone, and some are still on the roof.” Baoyong crouched toward the ground, sprang onto the roof, and chased after the thieves. The thieves knew that the Jia household had no men at home. Peering from the courtyard into Xichun’s room, they had seen a nun of surpassing beauty and instantly conceived lustful designs. Knowing that the main rooms held only women, who were moreover terrified, they were about to kick in the door when they heard men entering in pursuit, and so the whole band climbed onto the roof. Seeing that their pursuers were few, they still thought to resist. When one man suddenly came racing across the roof, the thieves, seeing him alone, cared even less and met him with their short weapons. But they were no match for Baoyong. With one mighty sweep of his staff, he knocked a thief from the roof. The thieves fled at full speed, crossing over the garden wall, while Baoyong pursued them along the roof. Unknown to him, several accomplices had already hidden in the garden to receive the stolen goods, much of which had been passed down to them. When the thieves came running back, these men raised their weapons to protect them. Seeing that only one man pursued, they presumed that one could not prevail against many and instead advanced to meet him. At the sight, Baoyong cried angrily, “You petty thieves! You dare come and fight me!” The thieves said, “One of our mates was struck down by them, and we do not know whether he is alive or dead. We may as well storm in and rescue him.” Baoyong attacked as soon as he heard them. The thieves brandished their weapons, and four or five of them surrounded him and began striking wildly. The men on watch outside also plucked up their courage and came rushing after them. Seeing that they could not overcome Baoyong, the thieves had no choice but to flee. Baoyong was about to pursue them when he stumbled over a chest. Stopping to look, he thought that the goods had not been lost and that the thieves were already far away, so he did not give chase. He told the others to bring lamps. There were only several empty chests on the ground, so he ordered them put away and prepared to hurry back to the main rooms. Unfamiliar with the paths, he wandered over to Xifeng’s quarters. Seeing the place ablaze with lamplight, he asked, “Have any thieves come in here?” From inside, Ping’er replied in a trembling voice, “We have not opened the door here either. We only heard people in the main rooms shouting that there were thieves. You had better go there.” Baoyong still could not find his way. At last he saw the night watchmen approaching in the distance and followed them to the main rooms.

p.src: Presently Jia Yun and Lin Zhixiao both came in and discovered that a burglary had taken place. Everyone anxiously went inside to take stock. The old lady's door stood wide open; by the light of a lamp they saw that the lock had been twisted apart, and upon entering found the chests and cupboards open. They berated the women on night duty: “Are you all dead? Did you not know when the thieves came in?” The night-watch women wept as they replied, “Several of us take turns keeping watch. We were responsible for the second and third watches and never stopped walking back and forth. The others take the fourth and fifth watches, after our shift ends. We merely heard them raise the alarm but did not see a single person. We hurried over to look, only to find that the things had already disappeared—we do not know when. Please, masters, question those responsible for the fourth and fifth watches.” Lin Zhixiao said, “Every one of you deserves to die. We shall deal with you later. Let us first inspect all the other places.” The men on night duty led them to Madam You's quarters, where the door was tightly shut. Several voices answered from within, “We were frightened to death!” Lin Zhixiao asked, “Has nothing been stolen here?” Only then did those inside open the door and reply, “Nothing has been stolen here.” Lin Zhixiao led the others into Xichun's courtyard, where they heard voices inside crying, “This is terrible! The young lady has been frightened senseless. Please wake up, miss!” Lin Zhixiao ordered them to open the door and asked what had happened. An old woman inside opened the door and said, “The thieves fought here and terrified our young lady out of her senses. Fortunately, Mistress Miao and Caiping managed to revive her. Nothing has been lost.” Lin Zhixiao asked, “How did the thieves come to be fighting?” One of the men on night duty said, “Luckily, Master Bao climbed onto the roof and drove the thieves away. We even heard that he struck one of them down.” Bao Yong said, “He is over by the garden gate.” Jia Yun and the others went over and indeed found a man lying dead on the ground. On closer inspection, he appeared to be Zhou Rui's godson. Everyone was astonished at the sight. They assigned one man to guard the body and two more to watch the front and rear gates, both of which remained locked as before.

p.src: Lin Zhixiao then ordered the gate opened and sent word to the garrison officer, who came at once to investigate. Following the thieves' tracks, they determined that the intruders had climbed onto the roof from the rear passage. The trail reached the roof of the western courtyard, where the tiles had been badly smashed, and continued all the way out through the rear garden. All the night watchmen declared in unison, “These were not mere thieves but armed bandits.” The garrison officer retorted irritably, “They neither carried torches nor brandished weapons, so how can you call it armed robbery?” The night watchmen said, “When we chased them, they hurled roof tiles down at us, so we could not get close. Fortunately, our man Bao climbed onto the roof and drove them back. When he pursued them into the garden, several more thieves actually fought with Bao. Only when they proved no match for him did they all flee.” The garrison officer said, “There you are again! If they were truly armed bandits, how could they have failed to defeat one of your men? Enough talk. Quickly determine exactly what was lost and submit an inventory; then we shall make our report.”

The garrison officer said, “There you are again! If they were truly armed bandits, how could they have failed to defeat one of your men?
Enough talk. Quickly determine exactly what was lost and submit an inventory; then we shall make our report.”

p.src: Jia Yun and the others returned to the main apartments, where they found Xifeng, ill though she was, already there, supported by attendants; Xichun had also come. Jia Yun paid his respects to Xifeng and inquired after Xichun. They all tried to ascertain what had been stolen. But Yuanyang was dead, and Amber and the others had gone to accompany the funeral procession. All the possessions belonged to the old lady and had never been inventoried, merely placed under seal, so where could they even begin their investigation now? Everyone said, “There were a great many things in those chests and cupboards, yet now they are empty. It could not have taken a short time to steal them all. What were those night-watch women doing? Besides, the thief who was killed was Zhou Rui's godson. They must all have been in league with one another.” When Xifeng heard this, her eyes grew fixed with fury, and she said, “Tie up all those night-watch women and hand them over to the garrison for interrogation.” They all cried out in misery, knelt on the ground, and begged for mercy. How they were dealt with, and whether the missing property was ever recovered, will be told in the next chapter.
